localPreparation.prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create one independent hypothetical local landscape on Kerberos, Pluto's small irregular bilobed moon, wide 16:9 approximately 1672 by 941. Sober photorealistic scientific illustration of independently invented pale grey fine-grained regolith, scattered angular blocks, shallow irregular depressions and a gently uneven low horizon. Do not depict the whole body's bilobed silhouette as a measured local horizon: its fitted ellipsoid is a poor global approximation and site normals are unknown. Brightness, grain sizes, grey colour, material chemistry and fractions, relief, illumination and exposure are artistic assumptions; inferred ice-rich reflectance is not a measured local material map. Low oblique light. Almost black empty sky is assumed transparency, not measured atmospheric absence. No astronomical disks, Sun, Pluto, Charon, other planets or stars, so no angular/raster-size claim. This is NOT a reconstruction of LORRI pixel blocks, a dated New Horizons photograph, observed crater or mapped site. Kerberos rotates nonsynchronously; no permanent Pluto-facing location. No haze, atmosphere in the foreground, plumes, liquids, oceans, biology, people, spacecraft, structures or survivable landing. Never copy, recolour or reuse a Moon, Mars, Pluto, Charon, Nix, Hydra, asteroid or any observed body's map. No reference images. Legible unobtrusive footer exactly 'IMAGINED · LOCAL KERBEROS'; smaller line 'Terrain, materials and lighting are assumed'. Independently composed terrain and subdued natural grey palette.
